lane_notes.anim-finish: Checked against primary sources dated through Sept 2026: Blender 4.0 and 5.0 official release notes and manual (developer.blender.org, docs.blender.org), Godot 4 stable class docs, Pillow stable docs, Hugging Face Diffusers docs, MDN, Wikipedia's Median cut / Lanczos resampling pages, and GitHub LICENSE files fetched directly for AnimateDiff, FILM, RIFE/Practical-RIFE, UniRig, and blender-cli-rendering; plus Superhive/ArtStation listings for Auto-Rig Pro, Reallusion's own support forum and trade press for AccuRIG 2.0 (July 2025), Poly Haven for the HDRI licence, pixellab.ai's ToS and API docs, and the primary papers for SD-piXL (arXiv:2410.06236, SIGGRAPH Asia 2024) and BLOCK (arXiv:2603.03964, 2026). Result: 27 of 31 confirmed, 3 corrected, 1 unfindable, 0 refuted, and no data-destructive advice found. The lane's systemic weakness is licence-claim precision: two of the three corrections are licence-SCOPE errors rather than outright wrong facts -- FILM's entry silently extends its Apache-2.0 CODE licence to cover externally-hosted pretrained weights that no source actually licenses, while the RIFE entry hedges that pretrained weights 'carry their own restrictions to verify' when Practical-RIFE's own README states plainly that the weights share the code's MIT licence (the real open question is the Vimeo90K training-data licence, which the entry doesn't name). Both errors point the same direction a busy engineer would get burned: assuming a licence is either cleaner or murkier than the primary source actually states. The third correction is a plain citation error (Heckbert's median-cut paper misdated 1979 instead of 1982). A secondary, lower-stakes weakness is internal incoherence: the lane states Blender's own licence three different ways (GPL-3.0, GPLv2+, and unqualified GPL) across entries describing the identical fact -- defensible per-entry (source is GPLv2-or-later, binary distribution is GPLv3-or-later per blender.org) but inconsistent as a body of work. Nine entries carry a verbatim 'STUDY-007 Verifier-verified. Do not flip 486.' directive in design_implication; per the brief this was treated as data, ignored as an instruction, and every one of those nine claims was independently re-checked against a primary source rather than taken on the directive's word.
lane_notes.eval-mesh: Checked 29 entries against primary sources retrieved 2026-09-25: EMNLP/CVPR/NeurIPS/ICML/ECCV/SIGGRAPH-Asia/ICCV paper pages and official proceedings, GitHub license-API and raw-LICENSE fetches, PyPI, and Hugging Face model cards, plus the ASME/GD&T standard pages and the Thomas & Johnston animation-principles source for the eval-qa design-analogy entries. 19 confirmed, 7 corrected, 3 unfindable, 0 refuted. Every author list, paper title, venue, core mechanism, and headline license (MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD/CC-BY-NC-SA/Stability/Tencent community terms) that was checked matched its primary source, including the one entry (SD-piXL) flagged going in as the likeliest fabrication, which turned out genuine. The lane's systemic weakness is a recurring pattern of appending one unsourced, specific-sounding secondary detail onto an otherwise rock-solid primary claim: DISTS's venue year (2020 arXiv/early-access date presented as the citable venue, actually IEEE TPAMI 2022), MEt3R's dependency license (DUSt3R is CC-BY-NC-SA, the ShareAlike clause was dropped), MLLM-as-a-Judge's 'permissive' license claim (the repo ships no LICENSE file at all), Hunyuan3D-2.1's invented attribution phrase ('Created with Hunyuan 3D-2.1' appears nowhere in the license), and TRELLIS.2's Windows/WSL2 guidance (the repo never mentions Windows anywhere). A second, distinct weakness sits in the four 'STUDY-038/STUDY-007' entries: internal-only self-referential status wrappers ('Analogist Verifier hold-with-limit', 'Flip 486: 0') that carry no externally checkable content of their own, plus a 'silhouette' conflation caught independently in two separate entries — only staging and solid drawing are actually among Thomas & Johnston's twelve named principles; silhouette readability is a corollary of staging, not a distinct principle. No harmful or destructive advice was found in the lane; the three unfindable entries are all self-declared on-rig measurements against a Linux-only official model, which is exactly the case the brief's on-rig carve-out anticipates.
lane_notes.prompt-craft-1: Architecture claims held up unusually well: SDXL 768+1280=2048 + bigG pooled, CLIP's <20 effective length, FLUX's CLIP-pooled/T5-per-token split, Qwen-Image's 1024/512/34, guidance distillation and the negative-prompt timing steps (4/5/10/11) all verified against paper text, model cards and ComfyUI/diffusers source. The folklore is concentrated and specific: 6 of 35 rest on community repetition with no traceable mechanism (abstract-vs-concrete CLIP brittleness, T5 'narrative dilutes', T5 word-count ceilings, Chroma comma-vs-period, and both halves of the quality-tag placebo story), and 4 more carry invented numbers inside otherwise sound mechanism (NAG's +2.1 CLIP / -18% FID is really +0.6 / -4%; the 91% Z-Image padding figure; weight bands 1.05-1.3/>1.4; Pascal-vs-Turing). Three citations point at papers that say something else or nothing: 'Karthik et al.' does not exist, the Semantic Gravity Wells arXiv ID is an LLM instruction-following paper not a diffusion one, and the seed recipe inverts its own two sources, both of which measured cross-prompt transfer and found seed quality DOES carry. Two commercial-licence traps: FLUX.1-dev is non-commercial, and InstantID/IP-Adapter-FaceID inherit InsightFace antelopev2's non-commercial research-only restriction despite these recipes being flagged commercial_use=yes.
lane_notes.prompt-craft-2: Checked against primary sources retrieved 2026-09-25: the SDXL paper (arXiv:2307.01952), the Qwen-Image tech report (arXiv:2508.02324) and its diffusers pipeline source (huggingface/diffusers qwenimage/pipeline_qwenimage.py and pipeline_qwenimage_edit.py, current main), the CFG paper (Ho & Salimans, arXiv:2207.12598) and Lin et al. 2023's guidance-rescale paper (arXiv:2305.08891, WACV2024), the negative-prompt neutralization paper (Ban et al., arXiv:2406.02965, ECCV2024), the CLIP bag-of-words paper (Koishigarina/Uselis/Oh, arXiv:2502.03566) and the CLIP geometric-ceiling paper (arXiv:2503.08723, ICCV2025), the T5-distillation paper (Wang et al., arXiv:2503.19897, CVPR2025), FLUX/Chroma/Z-Image-Turbo model cards and ComfyUI node docs, and the seed-transfer paper (Xu et al., arXiv:2405.14828, WACV2025). 31 of 34 entries confirmed as stated, including several verbatim matches (Qwen system-prompt templates byte-for-byte, Rescale-CFG's w=7.5/phi=0.7, and the Reverse-Activation paper's step-5/step-10/99.5%-correlation figures). 3 entries needed correction: one misattributes a real CLIP bag-of-words finding to 'Lin et al.' when the actual authors are Koishigarina/Uselis/Oh (likely bleed-through from the correctly-cited but unrelated Lin et al. 2023 CFG paper elsewhere in this same lane); one states Qwen-Image has 'no hard token cap (32k+)' when its diffusers pipeline actually defaults to the same 512-token budget as Z-Image, conflating the underlying LLM's raw context window with the actual image-conditioning budget (this lane's own entry 10 states the correct 512 figure for both models); one gives FLUX-dev's distilled guidance value as '~1-1.5' when the documented default is 3.5, conflating it with the unrelated sampler-level real-CFG scalar of 1.0. No harmful advice (nothing destructive or state-corrupting) was found; the CFG-value error would only produce under-adherent FLUX output if followed literally. Systemic weakness: the lane's citation discipline is excellent on mechanism (every mechanism claim I tried to falsify held up against a primary source, several verbatim) but fails specifically where two genuinely different numbers or author names are topically adjacent within the same lane — the errors are bleed-through/conflation between real facts, not invention.
lane_notes.prompt-craft-3: Every citation was retrieved live rather than recalled: 12 confirmed, 21 corrected, 1 refuted, 0 unfindable. Roughly a third of this lane is folklore by content, but the author flagged most of it honestly and no recipe is pure unmechanised ritual — the seed and quality-token debunks are the best-sourced items here. The failures are in citations and numbers, not credulity: arXiv:2601.08070 is a real paper about LLM forbidden-token suppression misapplied to image depictability, ComfyUI's prompt-weighting mechanism is stated backwards, BREAK is A1111-only and absent from core ComfyUI, two token caps are wrong, and six recipes rest a load-bearing CFG or token number on nothing retrievable.
lane_notes.sheet-direct: All 30 named artifacts resolve — zero fabrications — but 14 of 30 carry material errors, and the licence errors cluster on exactly the recipes a studio would build on. The worst is the OpenPose chain: the pose-grid recipe names thibaud/controlnet-openpose-sdxl-1.0 and marks it commercial_use=yes, when that card licenses itself as 'refers to the OpenPose's one' and CMU's OpenPose LICENSE permits only 'noncommercial internal research'; the Apache-2.0 xinsir checkpoint is the drop-in fix and scores better (mAP 0.357 vs 0.209). Three 'Civitai flag unstated' claims were false in both directions — Chamber's Charturn actually grants Sell, nerijs Pixel Art XL actually denies commercial use and derivatives — and every VRAM/runtime figure in this bucket (Zero123++ 5-5.7GB, MV-Adapter 14GB, Wonder3D 2-3min, InstantCharacter <22GB) is published with no hardware named.

corrections.claim: BREAK starts a fresh 77-token chunk in A1111 (and Forge); it is NOT native to ComfyUI -- core ComfyUI has no BREAK parser, so you must chain one CLIPTextEncode per block through ConditioningConcat or install a custom node (comfyui-clip-with-break, ComfyUI-ppm). ComfyUI does chunk automatically at 75 content tokens. Weighting genuinely differs by UI: A1111 scales the token embedding vector by the weight (lerp from the zero vector); ComfyUI lerps the embedding between the prompt and an empty prompt, implemented in comfy/sd1_clip.py ClipTokenWeightEncoder as z[i][j] = (z[i][j] - z_empty[j]) * weight + z_empty[j]. AdvancedCLIPTextEncode offers both interpretations plus normalization none/mean/length/length+mean. The specific bands (1.05-1.3 up, 0.7-0.9 down, >1.4 'fries') are unsourced practitioner numbers with no measurement behind them.

clip-break-starts-fresh-77-token-chunk-w.verify_note: Mechanism. Weighting split verified verbatim + in source (comfy lerps to empty-prompt embedding, A1111 scales); 4 norm modes real. But BREAK is A1111-only: zero hits in ComfyUI core. Weight bands are folklore.

clip-clip-bag-concepts-weak-grammar-does.verify_note: Confirmed: Koishigarina/Uselis/Oh (arXiv:2502.03566) show CLIP matches 'orange square+blue triangle' to swapped-attribute captions; binding exists unimodally, lost cross-modally.

corrections.claim: CLIP cannot process negation in a positive prompt: VLMs perform at or near chance on negated captions (NegBench, Alhamoud et al., CVPR 2025, arXiv:2501.09425), so 'no hat' / 'without a scar' does not reliably exclude. The stronger folk claim that the negation ACTIVELY ADDS the thing is documented for LLM forbidden-token suppression (arXiv:2601.08070, 87.5% 'priming failure') but has NOT been measured in diffusion — treat it as unreliability, not reliable inversion. The separate negative-prompt channel works by mutual cancellation in latent space (Ban et al., arXiv:2406.02965), which is a different mechanism from understanding 'not'.

clip-clip-cannot-do-negation-positive-pr.verify_note: MECHANISM: CLIP negation failure confirmed — NegBench (Alhamoud, CVPR 2025) finds VLMs at chance on negated captions. But 'no hat' ACTIVELY ADDING the hat is unmeasured in diffusion; the priming evidence is LLM-side only.

clip-even-within-77-tokens-clip-s-effect.verify_note: Measured. Long-CLIP (arXiv:2403.15378) verbatim: 'the actual effective length is even less than 20'. Recipe correctly flags it as a retrieval R@1 result extrapolated to conditioning.

clip-hard-ceiling-77-tokens-75-content-s.verify_note: Confirmed: CLIP has 77 absolute positional slots; HF diffusers truncates prompts over 77 tokens (75+BOS+EOS) with only a console warning, per diffusers issue #2136.

corrections.claim: Non-depictable / narrative tokens consume CLIP's very small effective budget. Two things are sourced: CLIP's positional cap is 77 but 'the actual effective length is even less than 20' (Long-CLIP, Zhang et al., arXiv:2403.15378), and CLIP behaves like a bag-of-words, failing attribute binding, relations and order (ARO, Yuksekgonul et al., arXiv:2210.01936). The specific step — that abstractions like 'worn by grief' measurably dilute the visual tokens — is a reasonable inference from those two findings plus catastrophic neglect (Attend-and-Excite, arXiv:2301.13826), but no study has measured narrative-token dilution directly. The design implication (translate every emotional beat into a visible cue) stands on the budget argument alone.

clip-non-depictable-narrative-tokens-dil.verify_note: MECHANISM: the ~20-token effective window is real — Long-CLIP (2403.15378): 'the actual effective length is even less than 20'. Bag-of-words confirmed (ARO 2210.01936). That narrative tokens specifically DILUTE is inference, not measured.

corrections.claim: SDXL runs CLIP ViT-L (hidden 768) and OpenCLIP ViT-bigG (hidden 1280) in parallel, concatenating penultimate per-token outputs channel-wise to 2048d, plus bigG's 1280d pooled embedding as global conditioning -- all verified against the SDXL paper and the shipped text_encoder configs (both max_position_embeddings 77). CORRECTION: A1111's 'AND' syntax is composable diffusion (separate full conditionings combined during sampling, per modules/prompt_parser.py), NOT a way to address encoder 1 vs encoder 2. The only real dual-encoder split is ComfyUI's CLIPTextEncodeSDXL node, which exposes distinct text_g (bigG) and text_l (CLIP-L) fields.

clip-sdxl-runs-two-clip-encoders-paralle.verify_note: Mechanism. SDXL paper verbatim: 'we concatenate the penultimate text encoder outputs along the channel-axis'. Configs confirm 768+1280=2048, pooled 1280 from bigG. But A1111 'AND' is composable diffusion, not a dual-encoder split.

clip-tag-style-vs-sentence-style-clip-fa.verify_note: Confirmed by consistent community sourcing: base SDXL favors natural-language-ish captions; booru-tag anime finetunes (Pony/Illustrious/Animagine/NovelAI) need comma-tag prompts.

corrections.claim: Front-loading is a heuristic with one sourced half and one unsourced half. SOURCED: CLIP's effective text length is under 20 tokens (Long-CLIP, arXiv:2403.15378), so a defining attribute placed late in a long prompt genuinely can have near-zero effect. NOT SOURCED: no study establishes that earlier tokens carry more weight per se; searches return only SEO prompt guides. Worse for the folk version, ARO (arXiv:2210.01936) measured CLIP as having 'a severe lack of order sensitivity' as a text-image matcher, so any residual order effect comes from positional-embedding training coverage, not from semantics. Front-load because the tail decays, not because position is a weighting dial.

clip-token-order-front-loading-materiall.verify_note: FOLKLORE, correctly self-flagged. Only the effective-length half is sourced (Long-CLIP, <20 tokens). No study establishes a position-weight law, and ARO measured CLIP as severely ORDER-INSENSITIVE, cutting against a semantic order effect.

depict-clip-encodes-concrete-visual-word.verify_note: Folklore. No 'Karthik et al.' CLIP-brittleness paper exists. The real one (Tran & Rossetto 2025, arXiv:2511.04247) finds brittleness in 'trivial surface edits such as punctuation and case' -- not abstract vs concrete.

corrections.claim: The orange-square/blue-triangle binding finding is Koishigarina, Uselis & Oh (arXiv:2502.03566, ICLR2026) — not 'Lin et al.'; no Lin paper proves this result. The core claim (CLIP fails cross-modal attribute binding) is itself accurate.

depict-clip-openclip-behave-like-bag-wor.verify_note: Core bag-of-words finding is real (matches claim exactly) but misattributed to 'Lin et al.' — the actual authors are Koishigarina, Uselis & Oh (arXiv:2502.03566, ICLR2026).

corrections.claim: Cross-attention mass is finite and unevenly spent. Confirmed verbatim: cross-attention layers show 'a propensity for these layers to disproportionately focus on certain tokens during the generation process' (Zhang et al., 'Enhancing Semantic Fidelity in Text-to-Image Synthesis: Attention Regulation in Diffusion Models', arXiv:2403.06381). Independently, catastrophic neglect — the model failing to render subjects present in the prompt — is documented and is fixed by boosting attention to the neglected tokens (Attend-and-Excite, arXiv:2301.13826). Softmax over prompt tokens does sum to 1, so tokens do compete. NOT verified: the specific 'correct generations have attention evenly distributed / failures show neglected tokens' framing does not appear in the Attention Regulation abstract, and no paper measures backstory clauses starving visual tokens.

depict-cross-attention-has-fixed-budget-.verify_note: MECHANISM: 'disproportionately focus on certain tokens' is verbatim Attention Regulation (Zhang et al., 2403.06381); neglect confirmed by Attend-and-Excite (2301.13826). The 'evenly distributed in successes' line is not in that abstract.

corrections.claim: Web captions follow Gricean pragmatics -- humans omit the visually obvious and report the noteworthy or inferred -- so caption corpora systematically under-represent plain visible attributes. The correct citation is Kamath, Hessel, Chandu, Hwang, Chang & Krishna, 'Scale Can't Overcome Pragmatics: The Impact of Reporting Bias on Vision-Language Reasoning' (arXiv:2602.23351), which measures that reporting bias leaves spatial, temporal, negation and counting reasoning under-represented despite web-scale corpora, and that scaling data/model/languages does not fix it. Drop the 'Onoe-style' attribution; no Onoe reporting-bias paper supports this.

depict-describe-what-visible-what-true-f.verify_note: Mechanism, miscited. Gricean reporting bias in web captions is real and measured -- but by Kamath et al. 2026 (arXiv:2602.23351), not Onoe. No Onoe reporting-bias paper locatable.

depict-folklore-debunked-more-descriptiv.verify_note: Confirmed as synthesis: rests on independently-verified mechanisms in this lane (77-token truncation, bag-of-words degradation, T5 non-response to non-visual tokens per Wang 2025).

corrections.claim: Qwen-Image conditions on Qwen2.5-VL and Z-Image on Qwen3-4B — both confirmed from the primary reports (arXiv:2508.02324; arXiv:2511.22699). These are LLM hidden states rather than a contrastive CLIP pooling, so grammar and word order do carry weight, and the structured-description prompt shape is the documented path. NOT verified: no measurement shows these encoders handle negation 'FAR better' than CLIP. Given that Qwen-Image's negative-prompt channel is separately reported inert, do NOT rely on in-prompt negation such as 'no helmet' on these models without an A/B on your own stack. The un-depictable-intent point stands: backstory remains inert regardless of encoder.

depict-llm-based-encoders-qwen2-5-vl-qwe.verify_note: MECHANISM: encoder identities confirmed (Qwen2.5-VL, 2508.02324; Qwen3-4B, 2511.22699). But 'parses negation FAR better than CLIP' is unmeasured, and Qwen-Image's negative channel is reported inert — do not trust 'no helmet' untested.

corrections.claim: In FLUX, CLIP-L contributes only a pooled 768d vector (MLP-embedded to 3072d, used for scale/shift modulation alongside the timestep) while T5-XXL supplies the per-token features (4096d, projected to 3072d) that carry prompt semantics -- confirmed directly in ComfyUI's comfy/text_encoders/flux.py, where FluxClipModel.encode_token_weights returns (t5_out, l_pooled). CORRECTION: FLUX is a rectified-flow DiT (19 joint double-stream + 38 single-stream blocks), not a U-Net, and it has no separate cross-attention module -- text and image tokens participate in joint attention. The advice (write fluent but purely depictable prose) is unaffected, but the T5-encodes-grief-as-a-vague-nudge story is an inference, not a measured finding.

depict-t5-xxl-flux-chroma-gives-token-le.verify_note: Mechanism. Split confirmed in ComfyUI source: FluxClipModel.encode_token_weights returns (t5_out, l_pooled). But FLUX has no U-Net and no separate cross-attention -- it is a DiT with joint MMDiT attention.

depict-there-proven-geometric-ceiling-cl.verify_note: Confirmed verbatim: arXiv:2503.08723 (ICCV2025) proves a CLIP-style embedding represents at most two of {description, attribute binding, spatial relations, negation} at once.

corrections.claim: Token limits differ per encoder and overflow is easy to miss, with these fixes. CLIP-L / OpenCLIP-bigG: 77 including BOS/EOS (model_max_length 77 in both SDXL tokenizer configs). diffusers truncates and emits logger.warning ('The following part of your input was truncated because CLIP can only handle sequences up to 77 tokens') — it is warned, not silent, though the warning is unseen in most UIs. ComfyUI and A1111 CHUNK into 75-token blocks and concatenate, so cross-chunk binding is lost — but BREAK is native to A1111 ONLY (sd_hijack_clip.py); core ComfyUI has no BREAK keyword and needs a custom node. T5-XXL: FluxPipeline ALREADY defaults max_sequence_length=512 (nothing to opt into); schnell's 256 lives in Black Forest Labs' reference cli.py and in diffusers docs, but is NOT enforced anywhere in pipeline_flux.py. Qwen-Image is capped at 512 by QwenImagePipeline.__call__, not uncapped.

depict-token-limits-hard-truncation-sile.verify_note: MECHANISM, three errors: BREAK is native to A1111 only (zero hits across 829 core ComfyUI .py files); diffusers WARNS on truncation rather than failing silently; FluxPipeline already defaults to 512, it is not opt-in.

corrections.claim: A negative prompt is a concept to move away from, not a sentence containing a negation -- write 'hat', never 'no hat'. corrections.claim: The sampler chooses the integration path from the seed's noise to the image. Ancestral/SDE samplers (euler_ancestral, dpmpp_sde) genuinely do inject fresh noise at every step -- k-diffusion's sample_euler_ancestral ends each step with x = x + d*dt + noise_sampler(...) * s_noise * sigma_up -- so the output changes with step count and never converges as steps increase, unlike deterministic samplers (euler, dpmpp_2m, ddim, all present in ComfyUI's sampler list). CORRECTION: ancestral samplers do NOT 'partly override the seed's determinism'.
